name: Payday itself, salary landed and posted today: the occurrence is closed and every real bill is deducted once (G362)

expected.notes: Payday itself, Fri 30 Oct 2026, pay period last Friday, so the new period runs 30 Oct to Thu 26 Nov (next payday Fri 27 Nov, 28 days away, window days 0 to 27). The 3,000 salary (history 31 Jul, 28 Aug and 25 Sep, equal, monthly rhythm, largest credit on Barclays) is the steady salary. Barclays holds 4,200 (1,200 before pay + 3,000 landed) and HSBC holds 80. Real items in the period: Barclays standing order to HSBC 900 (Fri 30 Oct, day 0, own account, HSBC spendable), mortgage 1,100 (Mon 2 Nov, day 3), council tax 150 (Fri 6 Nov, day 7), phone 45 (Mon 16 Nov, day 17); HSBC home insurance 120 (Tue 10 Nov, day 11). The salary has landed in the balance AND posted as an Income credit dated today (G362). The occurrence expected today is closed by that credit (same account, within 15 percent, inside the lookback), so no salary occurrence is left in the period (the next one is 31 days away, outside it) and the closed one is listed as observed income instead: nothing is credited a second time. Left to spend: pool 4,200 + 80 = 4,280. The standing order moves money inside the pool, so both of its legs drop. 4,280 - 1,100 = 3,180; - 150 = 3,030; - 120 = 2,910; - 45 = 2,865. There is no income left to credit. The lowest point is the last figure, 2,865, below the opening 4,280. No buffer, set-aside, goal or card reserve, so Left to spend is 2,865 (the real bills, 1,415, are deducted once). Barclays walk: 4,200 - 900 (day 0) = 3,300; - 1,100 = 2,200; - 150 = 2,050; - 45 = 2,005. After payments 2,005, low point 2,005, Spend from 2,005 (below the pool). HSBC walk: 80; the 900 standing order is credited on day 0 because its source is still at 3,300, at or above zero, after its own day-0 items (G360 funded rule), so 980; - 120 = 860. After payments 860; low point 80 (the opening balance is the lowest running balance); Spend from min(860, 80) = 80. Nobody is short, so no cover move; at risk 0. No payday plan: a salary credit has posted in this period, so the live plan has nothing left to recommend (G172) and none shows. G362 closes the occurrence out of upcoming_income into observed_income, and G374 lets that closed occurrence stand in for the salary candidate: the landed-salary test (_pp_salary_observed) finds the 3,000 credit on Barclays dated today, so the plan is suppressed. The unposted twin scenario still shows its plan, because there the salary has not posted.
